claim_reviews.conclusion: “count” meaning determine the number of items is clear and correctly aligned.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “menghitung” is a correct ordinary Indonesian equivalent for counting items.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “mengira” is a correct Malaysian Malay equivalent for counting; it is not exclusive, because “menghitung” is also accepted.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “different-common-word” is misleading because the two varieties share “menghitung” for this sense; use a shared-synonym or regional-preference relation.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false-friend contrast is applicable or necessary.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: No dedicated false-friend source was needed because the two forms are semantically aligned.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both Malay answers correctly express “count” in the stated sense. However, Malaysian Malay also uses “menghitung,” so the relation “different-common-word” overstates the contrast; this is better represented as a shared synonym with regional or usage preference. No false-friend contrast is needed.
